forehead.intro: Pain across the forehead often feels like a tight band or a dull pressure sitting just above the eyebrows, and many people assume it is a sinus problem or eye strain. It commonly builds through the afternoon and is noticeable in the evening after a long day of looking at screens. The muscles most often responsible are the sternocleidomastoid, the thick strap on the front of the neck that turns the head and holds it up in a forward position, and the suboccipitals, the small muscles at the base of the skull that fine-tune where the eyes are pointing. Both can send a steady ache forward into the forehead.
forehead.differs: A physician should first rule out head emergencies: a sudden worst-ever headache, headache with fever and stiff neck, confusion, vision loss or weakness means 911, not stretching. Forehead pain from muscle usually sits in a flat band and eases when the neck is gently moved. Temple pain tends to be one-sided and pulsing; behind-the-eye pain feels deeper and sharper; ear-area pain sits further back and often arrives with jaw clenching. Sinus pain usually comes with congestion and worsens bending forward.
forehead.scenario: Typical story: a remote worker in Sarasota spends the day on a laptop at the kitchen counter, head drifting forward toward the screen, then scrolls a phone on the couch in the evening. By dinner there is a tight band across the forehead most days of the week, with no congestion and no vision changes, and it fades on weekends spent outdoors.

temple.intro: Temple pain usually feels like a one-sided throb or a pressing ache just in front of the ear and above the cheekbone, sometimes reaching the eyebrow or the upper teeth. People often notice it after a stressful morning, on waking after a night of clenching, or late in the day when the shoulders have crept up toward the ears. The upper trapezius, the big shoulder-shrugging muscle, commonly refers a question-mark shaped ache up the side of the neck into the temple. The temporalis, the fan-shaped chewing muscle under the temple itself, adds a dull toothache-like quality when the jaw is tight.
temple.differs: A physician should first rule out head emergencies, including a sudden severe headache, a new headache with jaw pain and vision change in an older adult, fever, or weakness, which need urgent care. Muscle-related temple pain is usually tender to press directly over the temple or the top of the shoulder and shifts with jaw clenching. Forehead pain spreads across both sides; behind-the-eye pain feels deeper and worsens with eye movement; ear-area pain is lower and rarely throbs.
temple.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota professional drives an hour to and from the office, sits through long meetings with shoulders hunched, and wakes most mornings with a sore jaw. Mid-afternoon a steady one-sided ache sets in over the temple, with the same side of the upper shoulder feeling like a rock. It is better on vacation and worse during busy weeks.

behind-the-eye.intro: Pain behind or around the eye commonly feels like a deep, boring ache inside the socket or a pressure pushing the eye forward, and it is one of the complaints most often labelled a migraine or a sinus infection. It tends to appear after long periods of reading, driving or looking slightly upward at a monitor, and often starts at the base of the skull before travelling forward. The suboccipitals, the small muscles that steer the head on the top of the neck, are the usual source; the splenius muscles along the back of the neck and the SCM strap at the front also refer a deep ache into this spot.
behind-the-eye.differs: A physician should first rule out head and eye emergencies: a sudden worst-ever headache, a red painful eye with blurred vision or halos, double vision, or pain with fever and stiff neck all need urgent care. Muscle-referred eye pain is usually reproduced by pressing at the base of the skull and eases with gentle neck movement. Forehead pain is broader and more superficial, temple pain is pulsing and lateral, and ear-area pain sits behind rather than in front.
behind-the-eye.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident finishes a long book or binge-reads on a tablet propped low in the lap, chin tucked for hours. Later that evening a deep ache settles behind one eye along with a stiff upper neck. Eyes test fine, there is no congestion, and the pain fades after a night of good sleep but returns with the next long reading session.

around-the-ear.intro: Pain around the ear is often described as an earache, fullness, or a dull pressure in front of or behind the ear without any sign of infection. People frequently notice it when chewing, after a stressful stretch of jaw clenching, or on waking, and many have already had the ear itself checked and told it looks normal. The sternocleidomastoid, the strap muscle on the front of the neck, commonly refers ache and fullness into the ear. The masseter, the powerful chewing muscle on the cheek, sends pain just in front of the ear and into the back teeth, while the upper trapezius adds ache behind the ear.
around-the-ear.differs: A physician should first rule out an ear infection, hearing or balance disorders and head emergencies such as sudden severe headache, facial drooping or fever. Muscle-referred ear pain is usually provoked by pressing the cheek or front of the neck and changes with jaw position. Temple pain sits higher and throbs, forehead pain is broad and in front, behind-the-eye pain is deeper in the socket. True ear problems usually bring hearing change, discharge or dizziness that muscles rarely produce.
around-the-ear.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota snowbird returns for the season, starts a run of stressful phone calls held between shoulder and ear, and notices a nagging fullness and ache in one ear. The ear exam is clear. The ache flares with chewing gum or a tough steak, and the cheek and side of the neck on that side are tender to press.

base-of-skull.intro: Pain at the base of the skull typically feels like a deep, gripping ache right where the neck meets the head, often with a sense that the head is too heavy and a tight rim of tension spreading up over the back of the skull. It is usually worst after long periods of looking at a screen or steering wheel and when turning to look over a shoulder. The suboccipitals, the small muscles that nod and rotate the head on the top vertebra, are nearly always involved. The upper trapezius, the shoulder-shrugging muscle that also hangs the head from the shoulders, and the lower trapezius frequently add to the ache.
base-of-skull.differs: A physician should first rule out head and neck emergencies, including a sudden severe headache at the back of the head, headache with fever or stiff neck, or weakness and numbness after a fall or car accident. Muscle pain here is tender to press directly under the skull and eases with gentle chin tucks. Back-of-head pain sits higher on the bone, top-of-head pain is felt on the crown, and neck-joint pain is usually sharper and one-sided with turning.
base-of-skull.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota golfer plays three rounds a week, drives a cart with the head jutting forward, then watches television with a thick pillow pushing the head up. A heavy ache sets in at the base of the skull by evening and eases only when lying flat. There is no dizziness or vision change, just a sense that the head is hard to hold up.

back-of-head.intro: Pain at the back of the head is often felt as a spreading ache over the rounded part of the skull, with a tender scalp that makes brushing the hair or resting the head on a pillow uncomfortable. It is commonly noticed on waking after sleeping with the head propped too high, or after hours of concentrating with the neck held still. The occipitalis, the thin muscle that covers the back of the skull and helps move the scalp and raise the eyebrows, is the usual local source. The suboccipitals and the splenius muscles, which run up the back of the neck to turn the head, frequently feed an ache into the same area.
back-of-head.differs: A physician should first rule out head emergencies: a sudden worst-ever headache, headache after a head injury, headache with fever, confusion or weakness, or a new persistent headache in later life all need urgent evaluation. Muscle-related pain here comes with a tender scalp and tight neck muscles and changes with neck position. Base-of-skull pain sits lower and deeper, top-of-head pain is on the crown, and nerve irritation usually produces a sharp, electric or tingling quality.
back-of-head.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident on a long road trip north spends ten hours a day with the head pressed back against a headrest and the neck held rigid. A dull ache spreads over the back of the head with a scalp that feels bruised to the touch. It eases after a few days of normal movement and returns on the drive home.

top-of-head.intro: Pain on the top of the head is often described as pressure on the crown, like a cap that is too tight, or a sore spot that feels as if the skull itself hurts when touched. People tend to notice it late in the day, after hours of looking down at paperwork or a phone, or after sleeping with the head bent to one side. The splenius capitis and cervicis, the long muscles that run up the back of the neck and rotate and extend the head, are the most common source of pain referred to the crown. The sternocleidomastoid at the front of the neck can add a deeper ache to the top of the head.
top-of-head.differs: A physician should first rule out head emergencies, including a sudden severe headache, headache with fever, neck stiffness, vision change or weakness, and any new headache after a blow to the head. Muscle-referred crown pain usually comes with a stiff upper back of the neck and is reproduced by pressing there. Base-of-skull pain is low under the bone, back-of-head pain is on the curve of the skull, and scalp conditions usually show changes in the skin itself.
top-of-head.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota office worker spends the day switching between a monitor set too low and a phone held in the lap, head tilted down for hours. By late afternoon there is a tight pressure on the crown of the head and the back of the neck feels stiff when turning to check a blind spot on the drive home.

side-of-neck.intro: Pain on the side of the neck usually feels like a tight cord or a deep ache running from under the jaw toward the collarbone, often with a sense that turning the head one way is stiff or catchy. It is commonly noticed on waking, when checking a blind spot while driving, or at the end of a long day on the phone. The scalenes, the slender muscles that run from the side of the neck to the top ribs and help lift the chest for each breath, are the most frequent source. The levator scapulae, the muscle that hoists the shoulder blade up toward the ear, and the strap-like SCM at the front also contribute.
side-of-neck.differs: A physician should first rule out serious causes: neck pain with fever, swollen glands that persist, difficulty swallowing, or pain spreading into the jaw and arm with chest pressure or shortness of breath needs urgent attention. Side-of-neck muscle pain is tender to press and often sends tingling toward the thumb side of the hand. Front-of-neck pain sits over the windpipe, back-of-neck pain is along the spine, and neck-meets-shoulder pain is lower at the angle of the shoulder.
side-of-neck.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident who spends hours on calls holding the phone against one shoulder, breathing shallowly through a stressful season, develops a steady ache down the side of the neck with occasional tingling into the hand. Turning the head feels stiff in the morning and loosens through the day, and the ache returns with long stretches of talking.

front-of-neck.intro: Pain at the front of the neck often feels like a sore throat without the sickness, a tender cord beside the windpipe, or an ache that reaches toward the collarbone and the back of the jaw. People tend to notice it when swallowing, looking up to the ceiling, or lying on the back without a pillow. The sternocleidomastoid, the thick rope-like muscle that runs from behind the ear to the breastbone and turns and tilts the head, is the usual culprit, and it is remarkably sensitive to forward-head posture. The scalenes just behind it, which help lift the upper ribs with each breath, add a deeper ache lower down.
front-of-neck.differs: A physician should first rule out throat, thyroid and heart problems: pain with fever, trouble swallowing or breathing, a lump, hoarseness, or any pain spreading from chest to neck with pressure, sweating or shortness of breath means urgent care. Muscle pain here is tender when the strap muscle is gently pinched and shifts with head rotation. Side-of-neck pain is more lateral and often tingles into the hand, while back-of-neck and neck-meets-shoulder pain sit well behind the ear line.
front-of-neck.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident paints a ceiling or hangs hurricane shutters with the head tipped back for hours, then sleeps on a stack of pillows. A tender ache develops down the front of one side of the neck that aches when turning the head and swallowing. Throat looks normal, there is no fever, and pressing the cord-like muscle reproduces the familiar ache.

where-neck-meets-shoulder.intro: Pain at the angle where the neck meets the shoulder is the classic stiff neck: a deep, nagging ache in the corner between the neck and shoulder blade that makes turning the head to one side feel wooden and painful. It is often noticed first thing in the morning after sleeping awkwardly, or after a day of carrying a bag on one shoulder. The levator scapulae, the muscle that runs from the upper neck to the top inner corner of the shoulder blade and lifts the blade toward the ear, is the most common source. The upper trapezius, the big shrugging muscle, and the scalenes along the side of the neck commonly join in.
where-neck-meets-shoulder.differs: A physician should first rule out serious causes, including pain with arm weakness, numbness or loss of grip, or neck and shoulder pain alongside chest pressure or shortness of breath. Muscle pain in this corner is tender to press at the top inner edge of the shoulder blade and limits turning the head toward the painful side. Side-of-neck pain runs vertically higher up, back-of-neck pain sits on the spine, and shoulder-joint pain is felt lower, down over the arm, with reaching.
where-neck-meets-shoulder.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota pickleball player carries a heavy gear bag on one shoulder to morning games, spends afternoons at a laptop, and sleeps on the stomach with the head turned. One morning the neck is locked and a deep ache sits at the corner of the neck and shoulder, worst when checking traffic. It loosens with movement and returns each night.

back-of-neck.intro: Pain in the back of the neck usually feels like a stiff, aching column running from the hairline down to the shoulders, often with a sense that the head is heavy and that looking up or checking a blind spot is grinding and slow. People commonly notice it on waking after sleeping on a tall pillow, after a long day looking down at a phone or tablet, or at the end of a drive. The splenius muscles, the long straps that run up the back of the neck and extend and turn the head, and the suboccipitals, the small muscles at the top that fine-tune head position, are the most frequent sources. The levator scapulae and upper trapezius add ache lower down toward the shoulders.
back-of-neck.differs: A physician should first rule out neck emergencies, including neck pain with fever and stiffness, pain after a car accident or fall, sudden severe headache, or arm weakness, numbness or trouble with balance. Muscle pain here is tender along the back of the neck and eases with gentle chin tucks and warmth. Side-of-neck pain runs down toward the collarbone, front-of-neck pain sits over the windpipe, and neck-meets-shoulder pain is lower and out at the angle of the shoulder blade.
back-of-neck.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident spends evenings reading on a tablet in bed with the head propped forward on two pillows, then drives to work with the seat reclined and the chin jutting forward. A stiff column of ache settles into the back of the neck every morning and slowly loosens by midday. Arms feel normal, and gentle chin tucks ease the ache.

top-of-shoulder.intro: Pain on the top of the shoulder typically feels like a heavy, aching ridge running from the base of the neck out toward the point of the shoulder, often described as carrying a backpack that never comes off. It is noticed when shoulders have been held up during stressful work, after carrying groceries or a child, or when reaching overhead. The upper trapezius, the broad muscle that shrugs the shoulder and holds the head up, is the main source of the ache along the ridge. The supraspinatus, the rotator cuff muscle tucked under the top of the shoulder blade that starts the arm lifting out to the side, adds a deeper ache toward the point.
top-of-shoulder.differs: A physician should first rule out heart and lung causes when shoulder-top pain comes with chest pressure, shortness of breath, sweating or exertion, and gallbladder or diaphragm problems when it follows meals. Muscle pain here is tender to pinch along the ridge and eases when the shoulder is supported. Neck-origin pain usually worsens with turning the head, while a rotator cuff or joint problem hurts more with lifting the arm out to the side and may be weak.
top-of-shoulder.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota boater spends weekends hauling lines and coolers, then returns to a desk where the shoulders creep up toward the ears during a busy week. A heavy ache settles along the top of one shoulder, with a hard knot that is tender to the thumb. It is worst in the evening and better after a warm shower and a few shoulder rolls.

front-of-chest.intro: Pain in the front of the chest from muscle usually feels like a dull, aching soreness or tightness over the breastbone or upper pec, sometimes running down the inner arm, and it is often worse when pressing on the area, reaching across the body or taking a deep stretch. People tend to notice it after push-ups or heavy lifting, long hours hunched over a keyboard, or sleeping curled on one side. The pectoralis major, the fan-shaped chest muscle that pulls the arm forward and across, and the pectoralis minor, the small muscle beneath it that tips the shoulder blade forward, are the most common sources. The scalenes in the neck can add a deeper ache.
front-of-chest.differs: A physician must first rule out heart, lung and other chest emergencies: chest pain with pressure or squeezing, shortness of breath, sweating, nausea, pain spreading to the jaw or arm, or pain brought on by exertion is a 911 call, not a muscle problem. Muscle chest pain is reproduced by pressing on the chest wall and by stretching the arm back. Rib-side pain is lateral and breath-related, along-one-rib pain follows a single rib, and abdominal-wall pain sits below the rib cage.
front-of-chest.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident restarts a gym routine after the summer away, does a heavy chest day, then spends the week driving and typing with rounded shoulders. A deep aching tightness settles over the front of the chest and reaches down the inner arm. A physician's check is clear, the chest wall is tender to press, and stretching the arm back reproduces the familiar ache.

side-of-ribs.intro: Pain on the side of the ribs often feels like a persistent stitch or a sharp catch along the rib cage under the armpit, worse when breathing deeply, coughing, laughing or twisting to look behind. People notice it after a run, a bout of coughing, a long paddle, or reaching repeatedly across the body. The serratus anterior, the saw-toothed muscle that wraps the side of the ribs and pulls the shoulder blade forward with each reach or punch, is the most common source. The intercostals, the thin muscles between the ribs that expand and squeeze the chest for breathing, and the latissimus dorsi along the side of the back can add to the ache.
side-of-ribs.differs: A physician must first rule out heart, lung and abdominal emergencies: side-of-rib pain with shortness of breath, fever, cough with blood, a sudden sharp pain when breathing, or pain after a fall needs urgent assessment. Muscle pain here is tender to press between or over the ribs and reproduced by a deep breath plus a twist. Front-of-chest pain sits over the breastbone, along-one-rib pain follows a single rib line, and abdominal pain is below the cage and tied to digestion.
side-of-ribs.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota paddleboarder or kayaker heads out for a long session after months off, twisting and reaching with every stroke. Over the next two days a stitch-like ache sets in along the side of the ribs that catches with every deep breath and when rolling over in bed. Breathing itself is fine, and pressing between the ribs finds a tender spot.

along-one-rib.intro: Pain along one rib usually feels like a thin line of sharp or burning ache that follows the curve of a single rib from the back toward the front, often catching with a deep breath, a cough, a sneeze or a twist. People notice it after a long coughing illness, a heavy lift with a twist, or a hard tackle or fall. The intercostals, the small muscles between each pair of ribs that expand and compress the chest with every breath, are almost always the source. The serratus anterior, the muscle that hugs the side of the rib cage and pulls the shoulder blade forward, can add a wider ache near the side.
along-one-rib.differs: A physician must first rule out heart, lung and other emergencies: rib pain with shortness of breath, fever, a cough bringing up blood, chest pressure, or pain after a significant fall needs urgent care, and a blistering rash along one rib suggests shingles. Muscle pain here is tender to press along the rib and reproduced by a deep breath and twist. Side-of-rib pain is broader under the arm, front-of-chest pain is central, and abdominal pain sits below the rib cage and ties to eating.
along-one-rib.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota gardener spends a weekend hauling mulch bags and twisting to dump them, then catches a cold with a hard cough. A sharp line of pain develops along one lower rib that catches with every sneeze and when reaching up into a cabinet. Breathing is otherwise normal, there is no rash, and pressing along the rib finds a tender streak.

side-of-abdomen.intro: Pain in the belly or side of the abdomen from muscle often feels like a dull, aching soreness or a pulling sensation in the abdominal wall, sometimes sharp when sitting up from lying down, coughing, or twisting. It is commonly noticed after a new core workout, a long bout of coughing, or heavy yard work, and it can mimic heartburn or a side stitch. The external oblique, the broad muscle that wraps the side of the trunk and rotates and bends the body, is the usual local source. The psoas, the deep hip-flexor that runs from the low back through the pelvis, and the lower intercostals between the ribs can also refer ache to this area.
side-of-abdomen.differs: A physician must first rule out abdominal and other emergencies: belly pain with fever, vomiting, blood in the stool or urine, a rigid tender abdomen, a pulsing mass, or pain with chest pressure or shortness of breath needs urgent care, and appendicitis, hernia, kidney and gallbladder problems should be excluded. Muscle pain in the wall becomes more tender when the abdominals are tensed by lifting the head, while organ pain usually does not. Side-of-rib pain is up on the cage, along-one-rib pain follows a rib, front-of-chest pain is above the breastbone.
side-of-abdomen.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident starts a new core class and planks and twists hard on the first day, then spends the weekend pulling weeds and lifting pots. A deep ache sets in along one side of the belly that sharpens when sitting up in bed and coughing. Digestion is normal, there is no fever, and tensing the abs makes the spot more tender to press.

under-collarbone.intro: Pain under the collarbone usually feels like a deep, tender ache just below the bone, sometimes with a sense of fullness or tingling running down the front of the arm into the thumb and index finger. People notice it after wearing a heavy backpack or purse strap, carrying a sleeping child, or long hours with the shoulders rolled forward. The subclavius, a small muscle hidden under the collarbone that anchors it to the first rib, is the most common local source. The upper part of the pectoralis major, the chest muscle that pulls the arm forward, and the scalenes in the neck can add aching and tingling along the same path.
under-collarbone.differs: A physician should first rule out heart and lung problems: pain under the collarbone with chest pressure, shortness of breath, sweating or exertion needs urgent care, and swelling or color change in the arm needs prompt assessment. Muscle pain here is tender to press right under the bone and eases when the shoulder is pulled back. Front-of-shoulder pain is further out over the joint, outside-of-shoulder pain is over the deltoid, and deep joint pain feels inside with overhead reaching.
under-collarbone.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota parent carries a toddler on one hip and a heavy diaper bag on the opposite shoulder for months. A deep ache develops under the collarbone on the bag side, with occasional tingling into the thumb and index finger by evening. Pressing just beneath the collarbone reproduces the ache, and sleeping on that side makes the morning worse.

front-of-shoulder.intro: Pain in the front of the shoulder commonly feels like a deep ache or a sharp pinch at the front of the joint, worse when reaching behind the back, putting on a jacket, or lying on that side at night. People often notice it after an overhead project, a new weightlifting program, or weeks of sleeping with the arm tucked under the pillow. The infraspinatus, the rotator cuff muscle on the back of the shoulder blade that rotates the arm outward, is a surprising but frequent source of pain felt in the front. The anterior deltoid and the long head of the biceps, the muscles that lift the arm forward and help bend the elbow, add a more local ache.
front-of-shoulder.differs: A physician should first rule out a labral tear, fracture or dislocation after a fall, and heart or lung causes when pain comes with chest pressure or shortness of breath. Muscle-referred front-shoulder pain is often reproduced by pressing the back of the shoulder blade, while a biceps tendon problem is tender right in the groove. Under-collarbone pain sits higher and medial, outside-of-shoulder pain is over the deltoid, and deep joint pain feels inside with a catching or locking quality.
front-of-shoulder.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident repaints a lanai ceiling over a long weekend, arms overhead for hours, then sleeps on that side. A deep ache settles into the front of the shoulder that stabs when reaching back to grab a seatbelt or fasten a bra. Pressing on the back of the shoulder blade reproduces the front ache, and the shoulder is otherwise stable.

outside-of-shoulder.intro: Pain on the outside of the shoulder or upper arm typically feels like a deep ache over the rounded cap of the shoulder that runs down the side of the arm toward the elbow, often making it hard to find a comfortable sleeping position. People notice it when lifting the arm out to the side, reaching into the back seat, or carrying a bag with a straight arm. The supraspinatus, the rotator cuff muscle that starts the arm lifting sideways, is the most common deep source. The lateral deltoid, the muscle that forms the cap of the shoulder and lifts the arm out, and the infraspinatus behind it both refer pain down the outer arm.
outside-of-shoulder.differs: A physician should first rule out a rotator cuff tear, fracture or dislocation when pain follows a fall or the arm cannot be lifted, and heart causes when pain comes with chest pressure or shortness of breath. Muscle pain on the outer shoulder is tender to press on the deltoid and usually keeps full strength. Front-of-shoulder pain hurts reaching behind, under-collarbone pain is inner and higher, and deep joint pain feels inside with catching, while a neck nerve problem adds numbness.
outside-of-shoulder.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota pickleball player ramps up to daily games, hitting hundreds of overhead and side-arm shots, and starts carrying a heavy paddle bag on the same side. A deep ache sets into the outside of the shoulder that wakes them when rolling onto it at night and aches when lifting a coffee cup out to the side. Strength is fine and the arm moves fully.

deep-shoulder-joint.intro: Pain deep inside the shoulder joint is usually described as an ache that cannot be pointed to, as if it sits in the middle of the ball and socket, sometimes with a sense of stiffness or a vague catch when reaching overhead or behind the back. People tend to notice it when reaching into a high cabinet, washing their hair, or sleeping on that side. The infraspinatus and supraspinatus, the two rotator cuff muscles on the back of the shoulder blade that steer the ball in the socket, refer deep aching into the joint. The subscapularis, the rotator cuff muscle on the front of the blade, adds the stiff, frozen-shoulder quality.
deep-shoulder-joint.differs: A physician should first rule out a rotator cuff tear, labral injury, frozen shoulder, arthritis or infection, especially when the joint is hot, swollen or badly restricted after injury. Muscle-referred deep pain usually improves when the shoulder blade is supported and the tender spots on the blade are pressed. Front-of-shoulder pain is more surface and pinchy, outside-of-shoulder pain is over the deltoid, and under-collarbone pain sits high and inner. Joint problems often click, lock or lose motion.
deep-shoulder-joint.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota golfer with a new swing coach increases range time sharply, then adds overhead fishing casts on the weekend. A deep ache settles inside the shoulder joint that is hard to localize, worst reaching behind to tuck in a shirt and when lying on that side. The shoulder still moves fully, and pressing the tender back of the shoulder blade echoes the deep ache.

back-of-upper-arm.intro: Pain in the back of the upper arm usually feels like a deep, dull ache running from the back of the shoulder down toward the elbow, sometimes with a sense of heaviness or weakness when pushing up from a chair or reaching overhead. People notice it after push-ups, dips, a long day of hammering or pruning, or hours of leaning on an elbow at a desk. The triceps, the three-headed muscle that straightens the elbow and locks the arm out when pushing, is the most frequent local source. The teres major and subscapularis, muscles on the shoulder blade that pull the arm down and rotate it inward, refer an ache down the same line.
back-of-upper-arm.differs: A physician should first rule out a nerve problem when pain comes with numbness, tingling or weakness, a fracture or tendon rupture after a fall or heavy lift, and heart causes if arm pain arrives with chest pressure or shortness of breath. Muscle pain here is tender to pinch in the triceps and worse pushing against resistance. Back-of-shoulder pain stays up near the joint, shoulder-blade pain is on the flat bone itself, and neck-origin pain changes with head position.
back-of-upper-arm.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident spends a weekend trimming palms with loppers, arms held up and pushing repeatedly, then leans on an elbow at a laptop all week. A deep ache develops down the back of the upper arm that burns when pushing out of a low beach chair or reaching to the top shelf. The hand has full feeling, and pinching the triceps finds a sore band.

back-of-shoulder.intro: Pain in the back of the shoulder often feels like a focused, deep ache just behind the shoulder joint, as if a thumb is pressing into it, worse when reaching forward across the body, pulling a door open, or sleeping with the arm stretched forward. People notice it after rowing, swimming, backhand shots, or a long day driving with hands high on the wheel. The posterior deltoid, the back part of the shoulder cap that pulls the arm backward, and the teres minor, the small rotator cuff muscle at the back of the joint that rotates the arm outward, are the most common sources. The subscapularis and teres major can add a wider ache down the arm.
back-of-shoulder.differs: A physician should first rule out a rotator cuff tear, labral injury or fracture after a fall, and a neck nerve problem if pain comes with numbness or weakness. Muscle pain here is tender to press directly behind the joint and reproduced by reaching across the body. Back-of-upper-arm pain travels further down toward the elbow, shoulder-blade pain sits on the flat bone closer to the spine, and deep joint pain feels inside with overhead motion and locking.
back-of-shoulder.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota tennis player works on a two-handed backhand for several weeks and adds rowing at the gym, then drives a long distance with the arms held up on the wheel. A pinpoint deep ache develops at the back of one shoulder that catches when reaching across to the passenger seat. The shoulder moves fully and the sore spot can be found with one thumb.

on-shoulder-blade.intro: Pain on the shoulder blade commonly feels like a deep ache or burning spot on the flat of the bone itself, often with a sense that it needs to be pressed against a wall or doorframe for relief. People notice it after long stretches of mouse or phone use, after carrying a heavy bag, or on waking after sleeping on one side. The infraspinatus, the rotator cuff muscle that covers most of the blade and rotates the arm outward, is the most common source and is often tender over the bone. The middle and lower trapezius, the muscles that pull the blades back and down toward the spine, add a burning ache along the inner edge and top.
on-shoulder-blade.differs: A physician should first rule out heart, lung and gallbladder problems when blade pain comes with chest pressure, shortness of breath, sweating, fever or pain after fatty meals, and a neck nerve problem if pain brings tingling into the arm. Muscle pain here is tender to press over the blade and changes with arm position. Back-of-shoulder pain sits further out behind the joint, back-of-upper-arm pain runs down the arm, and between-the-blades pain is on the spine side of the bone.
on-shoulder-blade.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota real estate agent spends days driving between showings with one hand on the wheel and the other on a phone, then catches up on emails at night. A burning ache settles into the flat of one shoulder blade that begs to be pressed against a doorframe. The arm works normally, and pressing the blade reproduces the exact spot.

between-shoulder-blades.intro: Pain between the shoulder blades often feels like a burning, aching knot right alongside the spine, as if someone is holding a hot coin against the back, and it usually builds through the day with sitting. People notice it after long desk sessions, a long drive, or any period with rounded shoulders, and it often eases when the shoulders are pulled back. The rhomboid major, the muscle that connects the inner edge of the blade to the spine and squeezes the blades together, and the middle trapezius, the muscle that lies over it and does the same job, are the main sources. The scalenes in the neck often refer a deeper ache into the same area.
between-shoulder-blades.differs: A physician should first rule out heart, lung, aortic and gallbladder causes: pain between the blades with chest pressure, shortness of breath, sweating, a tearing sensation, fever or pain after meals needs urgent care. Muscle pain here is tender to press beside the spine and eases with a shoulder squeeze. Inner-edge-of-blade pain sits a little higher and out on the bone edge, bottom-tip pain is lower near the ribs, and a thoracic joint problem is usually sharp with a deep breath or twist.
between-shoulder-blades.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota remote worker relocates the office to a dining table and works ten-hour days on a laptop with no external monitor. By mid-afternoon a burning ache sits between the shoulder blades, relieved briefly by squeezing them together. The physician's check is clear, breathing is fine, and the spot is tender when pressed beside the spine.

inner-edge-of-shoulder-blade.intro: Pain along the inner edge of the shoulder blade usually feels like a sharp, nagging ache in a narrow strip right where the blade meets the upper back, sometimes with a stiff neck on the same side and a strong urge to dig a thumb or a ball into the spot. People notice it in the morning after sleeping with the head turned, after a long phone session, or when turning to reverse the car. The levator scapulae, the muscle that runs from the neck to the top inner corner of the blade and lifts the shoulder, and the rhomboid minor, which pins the upper edge of the blade to the spine, are the main sources.
inner-edge-of-shoulder-blade.differs: A physician should first rule out heart and lung causes when this pain comes with chest pressure or shortness of breath, and a neck nerve problem if it radiates into the arm with numbness or weakness. Muscle pain here is tender along the edge of the blade and worsens when turning the head toward the painful side. Between-the-blades pain sits lower and more central, bottom-tip pain is down near the ribs, and neck-joint pain is higher on the spine itself.
inner-edge-of-shoulder-blade.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident holds a phone against one shoulder through a week of long calls, then sleeps on the stomach with the head turned the same direction. A sharp ache develops along the inner edge of one shoulder blade with a neck that will not turn fully. The arm is strong and sensation is normal, and the ache eases when the shoulder is propped up.

bottom-of-shoulder-blade.intro: Pain at the bottom tip of the shoulder blade often feels like a deep, hard-to-reach ache right at the lowest point of the blade, sometimes with a sharp stitch when breathing deeply or reaching overhead. People notice it after pull-ups, swimming, paddling, or carrying heavy items at the side, and after a long coughing illness. The latissimus dorsi, the broad back muscle that pulls the arm down and back, attaches near this tip and commonly refers pain there. The serratus anterior, the muscle that wraps the side ribs and pulls the blade forward, and the iliocostalis along the outer back also send an ache to the lower blade.
bottom-of-shoulder-blade.differs: A physician should first rule out heart, lung and gallbladder causes: lower-blade pain with chest pressure, shortness of breath, fever, or pain after fatty meals, particularly on the right, needs urgent attention. Muscle pain here is tender to press at the tip of the blade and reproduced by pulling the arm down against resistance or a deep breath. Between-the-blades pain is higher and beside the spine, inner-edge pain is along the upper blade, and rib-joint pain is sharp with twisting.
bottom-of-shoulder-blade.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota kayaker increases weekend mileage and adds lat pulldowns at the gym, then carries heavy groceries in from the car. A deep ache lodges at the bottom tip of one shoulder blade that catches with a deep breath and when reaching into the back seat. Digestion is normal, breathing is fine, and the exact spot is tender when pressed.

front-of-elbow.intro: Pain at the front of the elbow usually feels like a deep ache or a tight pulling sensation in the crease, often with a sense of weakness when carrying a bag, curling a weight, or lifting a child. People notice it after a round of heavy lifting, a day of pulling weeds or hauling lines, or sleeping with the elbow bent tightly. The biceps, the two-headed muscle that bends the elbow and turns the palm up, is the most common source, and its tightness can refer ache down to the crease from the shoulder. The brachioradialis, the forearm muscle that lifts the hand when the thumb points up, adds ache at the outer front of the crease.
front-of-elbow.differs: A physician should first rule out a biceps tendon tear, especially after a sudden pop with bruising and a change in arm shape, and a nerve problem if pain comes with tingling into the hand. Muscle pain here is tender to pinch in the biceps and reproduced by curling against resistance. Point-of-elbow pain is at the back, forearm pain runs down toward the wrist, and golfer's elbow sits on the bony inner knob rather than in the soft crease.
front-of-elbow.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota boater spends a weekend hauling anchor and dock lines and lifting coolers, then starts a new arm day at the gym. A deep ache settles into the front of the elbow crease that pulls when carrying groceries or turning a stiff doorknob. There is no bruising or bulge in the arm, and pinching the biceps finds a sore band.

point-of-elbow.intro: Pain at the point of the elbow often feels like a deep ache or a sore, bruised feeling right on the bony tip, sometimes spreading to the inner elbow and faintly into the ring and little fingers. People notice it when leaning on the elbow at a desk or armrest, pushing up from a chair, or after a day of overhead work. The medial head of the triceps, the deep part of the three-headed muscle that straightens the arm and attaches at the point, is the most frequent source. The long head of the triceps, which runs from the shoulder blade down the back of the arm, adds a wider ache down the back of the arm and forearm.
point-of-elbow.differs: A physician should first rule out a fracture or bursitis if the tip is swollen, hot or follows a fall, and an ulnar nerve problem when there is persistent numbness in the ring and little fingers. Muscle pain here is tender in the triceps just above the point and worse straightening the arm against resistance. Front-of-elbow pain is in the soft crease, forearm pain runs toward the wrist, and golfer's elbow is tender on the inner bony knob rather than the tip.
point-of-elbow.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident drives long hours with the elbow planted on the console, then spends evenings at a laptop leaning on the same arm. A bruised-feeling ache develops at the point of the elbow that nags when pushing up out of a chair. There is no swelling or redness, the fingers feel normal, and pressing the triceps just above the tip reproduces the ache.

forearm.intro: Forearm pain usually feels like a tired, burning ache along the top or underside of the forearm, often with stiff fingers in the morning and a weaker, more fatigued grip by the end of the day. People notice it after a long session on a mouse, a stretch of heavy gripping such as pruning or paddling, or when pouring from a heavy kettle. The wrist and finger extensors, the muscles on the top of the forearm that lift the hand and fingers and stabilize the wrist during gripping, are the most common sources. The wrist flexors on the underside add ache when the palm side is overworked, and the scalenes in the neck can send pain down the forearm.
forearm.differs: A physician should first rule out a nerve problem such as carpal tunnel or a neck nerve when pain comes with numbness, tingling or night waking, and a fracture or compartment issue after trauma or sudden swelling. Muscle pain here is tender to press in the muscle belly and reproduced by gripping. Front-of-elbow pain sits in the crease above, point-of-elbow pain is at the back of the joint, and true tennis or golfer's elbow is tender right on the bony knobs.
forearm.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota pickleball player moves to daily games with a tight grip on the paddle and adds yard work pruning overgrown hedges. A burning ache sets into the top of the forearm, with stiff fingers in the morning and a grip that tires carrying groceries. Sensation in the hand is normal, and pressing the forearm muscles finds tender bands.

back-of-wrist.intro: Pain on the back of the hand or wrist often feels like a dull ache or a sharp twinge when bending the wrist back, pushing up from a chair, or doing a plank or push-up, sometimes with a stiff, puffy feeling in the fingers in the morning. People notice it after long days typing and mousing, a weekend of yard work, or a new upper-body program. The wrist extensors, the muscles on the top of the forearm that pull the hand back and hold the wrist steady when gripping, and the finger extensors, which lift the fingers, are the most common sources and refer pain down into the back of the hand. The scalenes and subscapularis can add ache from higher up.
back-of-wrist.differs: A physician should first rule out a fracture or ligament injury after a fall onto the hand, a ganglion cyst, arthritis in the wrist, or a nerve problem with numbness. Muscle-referred pain here is reproduced by pressing the top of the forearm and by resisted wrist extension, while the wrist itself is not swollen. Palm-side pain is on the underside with gripping, thumb and index finger pain sits on the thumb edge, and ring and little finger pain is on the opposite edge.
back-of-wrist.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident starts a home workout plan with daily planks and push-ups, then spends a weekend weeding and raking. An ache develops across the back of the wrist that twinges when pushing up from the floor or a low chair. There is no swelling or history of a fall, and pressing the top of the forearm reproduces the wrist ache.

palm-side-of-wrist.intro: Pain on the palm side of the wrist and hand usually feels like a deep ache in the heel of the hand or the inner wrist, sometimes with a cramping, tight feeling in the palm or a finger that catches when it straightens. People notice it after a long drive gripping the wheel, carrying heavy bags by the handles, using hand tools, or waking after sleeping with the wrist curled under. The wrist flexors, the muscles on the underside of the forearm that bend the wrist and anchor the grip, and the finger flexors, which curl the fingers, are the most frequent sources. The pectoralis minor and latissimus can add ache down the inner arm into the hand.
palm-side-of-wrist.differs: A physician should first rule out carpal tunnel syndrome and other nerve problems when there is numbness, tingling or night waking, and a fracture, ligament injury or arthritis after a fall or with swelling. Muscle pain here is tender in the underside of the forearm and worse gripping hard, with normal sensation. Back-of-wrist pain is on top with wrist extension, thumb and index finger pain hugs the thumb edge, and ring and little finger pain follows the outer edge of the hand.
palm-side-of-wrist.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident drives north and back for a family visit, gripping the wheel for many hours, then unloads suitcases and shops with heavy bags by the handles. A deep ache sets into the heel of the hand and inner wrist that cramps when wringing a towel. The fingers do not tingle, and pressing the underside of the forearm reproduces the hand ache.

thumb-and-index-finger.intro: Pain in the thumb and index finger often feels like an ache or tingling along the thumb side of the hand, in the web between thumb and index finger, or at the base of the thumb, and it is easily mistaken for carpal tunnel or arthritis. People notice it after hours of texting and scrolling, gripping a paddle or club, twisting jar lids, or using pruning shears. The scalenes in the neck, which lift the upper ribs during breathing and sit over the nerves to the arm, commonly refer pain and tingling to exactly these two fingers. The brachioradialis and supinator near the outer elbow, which turn the palm up and lift the hand, add ache into the thumb web.
thumb-and-index-finger.differs: A physician should first rule out carpal tunnel syndrome, thumb-base arthritis, De Quervain's tenosynovitis and a neck nerve problem, especially when there is constant numbness, weakness or wasting of the thumb muscles. Muscle-referred pain here comes and goes with neck or elbow position and is reproduced by pressing the side of the neck or outer forearm. Back-of-wrist pain is central on top, palm-side pain is in the heel of the hand, and ring and little finger pain is on the far edge.
thumb-and-index-finger.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident spends a season of long days on a phone, thumbs working constantly, then takes up pickleball with a tight grip. An ache and occasional tingling settle along the thumb and index finger, worse at the end of long days and when the neck is stiff. Grip strength is normal, and pressing the side of the neck or outer forearm brings on the familiar tingle.

ring-and-little-finger.intro: Pain in the ring and little finger typically feels like an ache, tingling or numb heaviness along the outer edge of the hand, sometimes running up the inner arm toward the elbow or armpit, and it often appears after sitting with rounded shoulders or sleeping with the arm overhead. People notice it after long typing sessions, leaning on the elbows, cycling, or carrying heavy bags. The pectoralis minor, the small chest muscle that tips the shoulder forward and sits over the nerves and vessels to the arm, and the latissimus dorsi, the broad back muscle under the armpit, commonly refer pain to these two fingers. The subscapularis and the lower pectoralis major also send ache down the inner arm.
ring-and-little-finger.differs: A physician should first rule out ulnar nerve entrapment at the elbow or wrist, a neck nerve problem, and heart causes when inner arm and finger pain comes with chest pressure, shortness of breath or sweating. Muscle-referred pain here shifts with shoulder posture and is reproduced by pressing under the collarbone or in the armpit, with normal sensation on testing. Thumb and index finger pain is on the opposite edge, palm-side pain is in the heel of the hand, and back-of-wrist pain is central on top.
ring-and-little-finger.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident spends weeks hunched over a laptop at a cafe with the shoulders rolled forward, then sleeps with the arm tucked overhead. The ring and little finger ache and tingle by late afternoon and on waking, easing when the chest is stretched. Sensation tests normal, and pressing the small chest muscle under the collarbone echoes the fingers.

beside-the-spine.intro: Pain right beside the spine in the low back usually feels like a deep, pinpoint ache or a sharp catch in a spot the size of a coin just to one side of the vertebrae, often worst when bending forward, standing up from a chair, or rolling over in bed. People notice it after a long drive, a weekend of lifting, or weeks of sitting slumped. The multifidus, the small deep muscles that stitch each vertebra to the next and steady the spine during every movement, are the most common source, and they weaken quickly when the back is sore. The psoas, the deep hip flexor that runs along the front of the lumbar spine, adds a vertical band of ache that makes standing tall hard after sitting.
beside-the-spine.differs: A physician should first rule out serious causes: low back pain with fever, unexplained weight loss, loss of bladder or bowel control, numbness in the saddle area, progressive leg weakness, or pain after a significant fall needs urgent care, and kidney problems when pain comes with urinary changes. Muscle pain here is tender to press right beside the spine and is not usually worse with a cough or sneeze. Flank pain sits further out to the side, SI pain is lower over the dimples of the pelvis, and tailbone pain is at the very bottom.
beside-the-spine.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident returns for the season after a long drive down, then spends the first weekend unpacking boxes and bending over garden beds. A deep pinpoint ache develops just to one side of the low spine that catches when straightening up from a chair. Legs are strong and sensation is normal, and pressing the spot beside the spine finds the exact tender point.

flank.intro: Pain in the flank or side of the low back often feels like a deep, dull ache between the lowest rib and the top of the pelvis, sometimes sharp when rolling over in bed, standing up from a chair, coughing or sneezing, and it can make people walk slightly bent to one side. It is commonly noticed after carrying a heavy load on one side, a long day of gardening, or a golf round with many twisting swings. The quadratus lumborum, the deep muscle that runs from the lowest rib to the pelvis and side-bends the trunk and hikes the hip, is the main source. The iliocostalis, the outer band of the back extensors, adds a vertical line of ache along the side.
flank.differs: A physician should first rule out kidney problems and other emergencies: flank pain with fever, painful or bloody urination, nausea, a pulsing mass, or pain that comes in intense waves needs urgent care. Muscle flank pain is tender to press deep between the rib and pelvis and is worse side-bending away from the painful side. Beside-the-spine pain is closer to the midline, SI pain is lower over the back of the pelvis, and tailbone pain is at the base of the spine.
flank.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota golfer plays several rounds in a week and carries a bag on one shoulder, then spends a day hauling mulch bags on the same hip. A deep ache settles into the flank between the ribs and pelvis that stabs when rolling out of bed or coughing. Urination is normal and there is no fever, and pressing deep into the side finds the tender muscle.

si-joint.intro: Pain at the SI joint and the back of the pelvis typically feels like a deep ache over one of the dimples at the top of the buttock, just to the side of the tailbone, often sharp when standing on one leg, climbing stairs, getting out of a car, or rolling over at night. People notice it during pregnancy, after a stumble, after a long run or walk on soft sand, or after weeks of sitting with a wallet in a back pocket. The quadratus lumborum, the deep side muscle that hikes the hip, and the gluteus medius, the side hip muscle that steadies the pelvis on every step, are the most common sources. The longissimus and iliacus also refer pain to this exact spot.
si-joint.differs: A physician should first rule out inflammatory arthritis of the SI joint, infection, fracture after a fall, and serious spinal causes with bladder or bowel change or leg weakness. Muscle-referred SI pain is tender in the muscles above and beside the joint and eases when the pelvis is supported with a belt or by lying down. Beside-the-spine pain is higher and central, flank pain is up between the rib and pelvis, and tailbone pain is lower and worse sitting directly on it.
si-joint.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident starts long morning beach walks in soft sand to get back into shape, then sits for hours in a low car seat. A deep ache settles over one dimple at the back of the pelvis that stabs when stepping out of the car or putting on pants standing. There is no fever or leg weakness, and the hip muscles above the joint are tender.

tailbone.intro: Tailbone pain usually feels like a deep ache or a sharp jab right at the bottom of the spine that is worst when sitting, especially on hard surfaces or when leaning back, and it often eases on standing or lying down. People notice it after a long stretch of sitting on a boat seat, a bicycle, or a hard bleacher, after a fall onto the buttocks, or after childbirth. The multifidus, the deep stabilizing muscles that run down to the sacrum and tailbone, commonly refer pinpoint pain here. The gluteus maximus, the large buttock muscle that powers hills and stairs, attaches alongside the tailbone and adds a broader ache with prolonged sitting and walking uphill.
tailbone.differs: A physician should first rule out a fracture or dislocation after a fall, infection or abscess, a pilonidal cyst, and rectal or pelvic organ problems, particularly with fever, bleeding or bowel change. Muscle-referred tailbone pain is tender in the buttock and sacrum muscles and eases when weight shifts to the thighs. Beside-the-spine pain is higher in the low back, flank pain is out to the side, and SI pain sits over the dimples a few inches up and to the side.
tailbone.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident spends long weekend days on a hard boat bench and weekdays in a low car seat, slumped back on the tailbone. A deep ache develops at the base of the spine that jabs when sitting down on a hard chair and eases on standing. There has been no fall and no fever, and the muscles beside the sacrum are tender.

middle-of-buttock.intro: Pain in the middle of the buttock often feels like a deep, hot ache in the center of one cheek, sometimes shooting down the back of the thigh toward the calf, and it is commonly called sciatica. It is noticed after long sitting, especially on a wallet or a hard seat, after a long drive, or after a sudden increase in walking or running. The piriformis, the small deep muscle that rotates the leg outward and runs right over the sciatic nerve, is a frequent source. The gluteus minimus, the smallest side hip muscle that steadies the pelvis on each step, is a classic sciatica look-alike, referring pain down the back or side of the leg to the ankle.
middle-of-buttock.differs: A physician should first rule out a true lumbar disc or nerve root problem, especially with numbness, progressive leg weakness, bladder or bowel change, or pain worse with coughing and sneezing, and hip joint disease. Muscle-referred buttock pain is tender deep in the cheek and reproduced by pressing there, with a normal nerve exam. Upper-buttock pain is along the belt line, outside-of-hip pain is lateral over the hip bone, and a hip joint problem usually hurts in the groin with rotation.
middle-of-buttock.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident drives eight hours with a thick wallet in the back pocket, then sits through a week of long meetings. A deep ache settles in the middle of one buttock that occasionally sends a line down the back of the thigh after sitting. Reflexes and strength are normal, coughing does not worsen it, and pressing deep into the buttock reproduces the leg ache.

upper-buttock.intro: Pain in the upper buttock at the belt line typically feels like a broad, dull ache just below the waistband along the top rim of the pelvis, sometimes sharp when standing on one leg, stepping up a curb, or getting out of bed, and it often makes people press their knuckles into the spot. People notice it after a long walk on soft sand, uneven golf course lies, a growth spurt in running, or weeks of standing with weight on one hip. The gluteus medius, the side hip muscle that keeps the pelvis level on every step, is the most common source. The quadratus lumborum, the deep side muscle above it, and the iliacus inside the pelvis also refer pain here.
upper-buttock.differs: A physician should first rule out serious spinal causes with leg weakness, numbness or bladder change, inflammatory SI joint arthritis, and kidney problems with urinary symptoms or fever. Muscle pain here is tender to press along the rim of the pelvis and worse standing on that leg. Middle-of-buttock pain sits lower in the center of the cheek and may shoot down the leg, outside-of-hip pain is lateral over the hip bone and hurts lying on it, and SI pain is a focused spot near the dimples.
upper-buttock.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident restarts running after a summer off and chooses the soft sand at the water's edge for several miles each morning. Within a couple of weeks a broad ache sets in along the belt line of one buttock that sharpens when stepping up a curb or standing on one leg to put on shoes. Legs are strong, and pressing the rim of the pelvis finds the tender band.

outside-of-hip.intro: Pain on the outside of the hip usually feels like a deep ache or a sharp tenderness over the bony point of the hip that makes lying on that side at night nearly impossible, sometimes spreading down the outer thigh toward the knee. People notice it when climbing stairs, getting up from a low chair, standing for long periods, or crossing the legs. The gluteus minimus, the small deep hip muscle that steadies the pelvis with each step, and the tensor fasciae latae, the muscle at the front-outer hip that tenses the long band down the thigh, are the most common sources. The gluteus medius and quadratus lumborum add ache from above and behind.
outside-of-hip.differs: A physician should first rule out hip joint arthritis, a stress fracture of the femoral neck in runners, and a lumbar nerve problem with numbness or weakness. Muscle-referred outer hip pain is tender to press on the soft tissue above and behind the hip bone and worse lying on that side, while hip joint disease usually hurts in the groin and limits rotation. Middle-of-buttock pain is behind in the center of the cheek, upper-buttock pain runs along the belt line above.
outside-of-hip.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident stands for long shifts on hard floors, starts a daily walking program on the sidewalk, and sleeps on the same side every night. A deep ache develops over the outside of one hip that wakes them whenever they roll onto it and aches on stairs. Groin motion is free and painless, and the soft tissue just above the hip bone is tender.

groin.intro: Groin pain often feels like a deep, pulling ache in the crease where the thigh meets the pelvis, sometimes spreading into the inner thigh, and it tends to be sharp when striding out, kicking, pivoting on the planted foot, or lifting the knee to get into a car. People notice it after a sudden sidestep in pickleball, long hours sitting, or a steep increase in running or cycling. The iliacus, the hip flexor that lines the inside of the pelvic bowl and lifts the thigh, is an overlooked but frequent source. The adductor longus and brevis, the inner thigh muscles that pull the legs together and steady the pelvis, add ache deep in the groin and down the inner thigh.
groin.differs: A physician should first rule out an inguinal hernia, hip joint problems such as a labral tear or arthritis, a stress fracture, and testicular, ovarian or urinary causes, especially with swelling, fever or a bulge that appears on straining. Muscle groin pain is tender to press in the inner thigh or deep in the hip crease and reproduced by squeezing the knees together. Front-of-hip-bone pain sits higher and more lateral on the bony point, while joint pain is deep with a pinch on bending and rotating the hip.
groin.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota pickleball player lunges hard for a wide shot during a tournament weekend, then sits for a long drive home. A deep pulling ache sets into the groin crease that catches when getting out of the car or crossing the leg to tie a shoe. There is no bulge or swelling, and squeezing a pillow between the knees reproduces the ache.

front-of-hip.intro: Pain at the front of the hip bone usually feels like a sharp or aching tenderness right on or just below the bony point at the front of the pelvis, sometimes with a sense of tightness when standing up tall after sitting, or a pinch when lifting the knee or taking a long stride. People notice it after long drives, hours at a desk, a steep increase in cycling or running, or a new program of sit-ups and leg raises. The rectus femoris, the long quadriceps muscle that runs from this bone down to the kneecap and both lifts the thigh and straightens the knee, is the most common source. The iliacus and TFL, the hip flexors beside it, add ache along the front of the hip.
front-of-hip.differs: A physician should first rule out hip joint problems such as a labral tear, impingement or arthritis, a stress fracture or avulsion in young athletes, and a hernia or abdominal cause with swelling or fever. Muscle pain here is tender right on the bony point and worse lifting the knee against resistance, while joint pain pinches deep in the groin with bending and rotation. Groin pain sits lower and more inward in the crease toward the inner thigh.
front-of-hip.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident adds a daily spin class and a set of hanging leg raises to an already desk-bound week. A sharp tenderness develops on the bony point at the front of one hip that pinches when lifting the knee to climb stairs and feels tight standing up from a long sit. Hip rotation is free, and pressing the bone itself reproduces the spot.

front-of-thigh.intro: Pain in the front of the thigh typically feels like a deep, heavy ache or a cramping tightness in the middle of the quadriceps, often worse climbing stairs, standing up from a low chair, or walking downhill, sometimes with a sense that the leg is tired and weak. People notice it after a long hike or beach walk, a heavy leg day, a sudden increase in cycling, or hours of sitting with the hips flexed. The rectus femoris and vastus intermedius, the two central quadriceps muscles that straighten the knee and lift the thigh with every step and stair, are the most common sources. The psoas and iliacus, the deep hip flexors, refer a vertical band of ache down the front of the thigh.
front-of-thigh.differs: A physician should first rule out a nerve problem such as meralgia paresthetica or a lumbar nerve root with numbness or burning skin, a deep vein clot with swelling, warmth and calf pain, and a muscle tear with bruising after a sprint. Muscle thigh pain is tender to press in the quad and reproduced by straightening the knee against resistance. Outside-of-thigh pain runs down the side toward the knee, and inner thigh pain tracks the adductors from the groin to the inner knee.
front-of-thigh.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident spends the summer sitting on long flights and in offices, then returns for the season with a sudden daily routine of walking the Legacy Trail and climbing condo stairs. A deep heavy ache settles into the front of the thigh that burns coming down stairs and when standing up from a low couch. There is no swelling or bruising, and pressing the quad finds tender bands.

outside-of-thigh.intro: Pain on the outside of the thigh often feels like a tight, burning band running from the hip down toward the outer knee, sometimes making it painful to lie on that side at night or to sit with the legs crossed. People notice it after long runs or walks on cambered roads or beach slopes, a steep increase in cycling, or weeks of standing with weight shifted onto one leg. The vastus lateralis, the large outer quadriceps muscle that straightens the knee, is the most common local source and often has tender bands along the whole outer thigh. The tensor fasciae latae at the front-outer hip and the gluteus minimus behind it refer a line of ache down the same side.
outside-of-thigh.differs: A physician should first rule out a nerve problem such as meralgia paresthetica or a lumbar nerve root, which bring numbness, burning skin or pins and needles rather than deep muscle ache, and a hip joint problem with groin pain and limited rotation. Muscle pain here is tender to press along the outer thigh and reproduced by lying on it. Front-of-thigh pain is central over the quad, inner thigh pain tracks the adductors from the groin.
outside-of-thigh.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident starts daily sunrise walks along the sloped hard-packed sand near the water, always facing the same direction, and sleeps on the same side. A tight burning band develops down the outside of one thigh that aches when lying on that side and when crossing the legs. Skin sensation is normal, and pressing the outer thigh finds tender ropes.

inner-thigh.intro: Pain in the inner thigh usually feels like a deep, pulling ache along the inside of the leg from the groin toward the inner knee, sometimes sharp when stepping sideways, getting out of a car, squeezing the legs together, or pushing off to change direction. People notice it after a quick lateral move in pickleball or tennis, a horseback ride, a long day of yard work in a wide stance, or a new round of lunges. The adductor longus and brevis, the inner thigh muscles that pull the legs together and steady the pelvis when standing on one leg, are the most common sources. The adductor magnus, the deep inner thigh muscle, and the vastus medialis near the knee add ache lower down.
inner-thigh.differs: A physician should first rule out an adductor tendon tear with bruising after a sudden pop, a hernia, a hip joint problem with deep groin pain and limited rotation, and a deep vein clot with swelling and warmth. Muscle pain here is tender to press along the inner thigh and reproduced by squeezing the knees together. Front-of-thigh pain is central over the quadriceps, outside-of-thigh pain runs down the lateral band from the hip, and groin pain sits higher in the crease.
inner-thigh.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident returns to pickleball after months away and plays several long sessions in a week, stretching wide for low shots. A deep pulling ache sets into one inner thigh that catches when stepping sideways out of the shower or swinging the leg into a car. There is no bruising or swelling, and squeezing a ball between the knees reproduces the ache.

back-of-thigh.intro: Pain in the back of the thigh often feels like a deep ache or a tight, cramping pull along the hamstring, sometimes running from under the buttock toward the back of the knee, and it is commonly noticed when sitting on a hard chair, bending forward to tie shoes, striding out on a walk, or standing up after a long drive. The hamstrings, the long muscles that bend the knee and pull the leg back with every stride, are the most common local source, particularly the inner hamstrings and the biceps femoris on the outside. The piriformis and gluteus minimus, deep hip muscles that sit over or near the sciatic nerve, refer a line of ache down the back of the thigh that is often mistaken for sciatica.
back-of-thigh.differs: A physician should first rule out a lumbar nerve root problem with numbness, progressive weakness or bladder change, a hamstring tear with bruising after a sprint, and a deep vein clot with swelling and warmth in the leg. Muscle pain here is tender to press in the hamstring or deep buttock and reproduced by bending the knee against resistance. Buttock-crease pain is focused high at the sit bone, and back-of-knee pain is low behind the joint rather than mid-thigh.
back-of-thigh.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident drives for hours to visit family, then jumps straight into a long beach walk and bends repeatedly to collect shells. A deep tight ache develops along the back of one thigh that pulls when sitting on a hard bench and when leaning forward to put on sandals. There is no bruising or swelling, and pressing the hamstring finds tender bands.

buttock-crease.intro: Pain in the buttock crease typically feels like a deep ache or a sharp, bruised sensation right at the sit bone where the buttock meets the back of the thigh, worst when sitting on a hard surface, driving, or stretching the leg forward. People notice it after a long cycling ride, hours on a hard chair or boat bench, repeated deep lunges or deadlifts, or an aggressive hamstring stretch. The inner hamstrings, the semitendinosus and semimembranosus that attach to the sit bone and bend the knee and extend the hip, are the most common source. The gluteus maximus, the big buttock muscle that powers hills and stairs and attaches nearby, adds a broader ache with long sitting.
buttock-crease.differs: A physician should first rule out a hamstring tendon tear or bony avulsion after a sudden pop, ischial bursitis with swelling, a lumbar nerve problem with numbness or weakness, and pelvic or rectal causes with fever or bowel change. Muscle pain here is tender exactly on the sit bone and worse sitting and stretching the hamstring. Back-of-thigh pain sits lower in the muscle belly, back-of-knee pain is well below behind the joint, and tailbone pain is central at the base of the spine.
buttock-crease.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota cyclist increases weekend mileage on a new bike with a hard saddle, then spends weekdays on a wooden dining chair working from home. A deep bruised ache develops right at the sit bone of one buttock that is sharpest sitting down and stretching the leg forward. There has been no sudden pop or bruising, and pressing the sit bone reproduces the spot.

behind-the-knee.intro: Pain behind the knee usually feels like a deep ache or a tight fullness in the hollow at the back of the joint, sometimes sharp when squatting, kneeling, walking downhill, descending stairs, or fully straightening the leg. People notice it after a hilly hike, a downhill run, long periods of standing with the knees locked, or a sudden increase in walking on the beach. The popliteus, the small muscle that unlocks the knee at the start of every step and steadies it on slopes, is a frequent and overlooked source. The gastrocnemius, the upper calf muscle that crosses the back of the knee, and the hamstrings that attach on either side of the hollow add aching and tightness.
behind-the-knee.differs: A physician should first rule out a deep vein clot with calf swelling, warmth and tenderness, a Baker's cyst with a visible lump, a meniscus or ligament injury with locking, giving way or swelling, and arterial problems in older adults. Muscle pain here is tender in the soft hollow or upper calf and reproduced by a deep squat or resisted knee bend. Back-of-thigh pain is higher in the hamstring belly, and buttock-crease pain is at the sit bone far above the knee.
behind-the-knee.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident visits the mountains for a week of hiking with long downhill stretches, then returns to flat beach walks with the knees locked straight. A deep ache settles into the hollow behind one knee that catches when squatting to the bottom drawer or stepping down a curb. There is no swelling, lump or locking, and pressing the soft hollow reproduces the ache.

below-kneecap.intro: Pain at the kneecap or just below it often feels like a deep ache around or behind the kneecap, a grinding sensation on stairs, or a sharp point at the top of the shin where the tendon attaches, and it tends to flare after sitting with the knee bent for a long time, such as in a movie or on a flight. People notice it on stairs, squatting, kneeling in the garden, or standing up from a low chair. The quadriceps, the four thigh muscles that straighten the knee and control how the kneecap tracks in its groove, are the most common source, particularly the rectus femoris and vastus medialis. Tight bands in the vastus lateralis and intermedius add pressure on the kneecap.
below-kneecap.differs: A physician should first rule out a fracture or patellar tendon injury after a fall or sudden pop, arthritis with swelling and warmth, a meniscus tear with locking, and infection with a hot red joint. Muscle-referred kneecap pain comes with tender quads and eases when the thigh is relaxed, without swelling. Inside-of-knee pain sits along the inner joint line and tracks the adductors and vastus medialis, while outside-of-knee pain follows the outer band from the hip.
below-kneecap.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident flies in for the season, sits for hours with the knees bent, then starts climbing condo stairs daily and kneeling to plant a garden. A deep ache sets in around and just below one kneecap that grinds coming down stairs and stiffens after sitting through dinner. There is no swelling or locking, and pressing the thigh muscles finds tender bands.

inside-of-knee.intro: Pain on the inside of the knee usually feels like a deep ache or a tender line along the inner joint, sometimes with a sense that the knee wants to buckle or give way on stairs, and it tends to flare after pivoting, side-stepping, or long walks on uneven ground. People notice it after pickleball or tennis, a long round of golf, kneeling in the garden, or a new lunge program. The vastus medialis, the teardrop quadriceps muscle just above the inner knee that locks the knee straight and steadies the kneecap, is the most common source. The adductors from the inner thigh and the inner hamstrings, which attach near the inner knee, add ache along the same side.
inside-of-knee.differs: A physician should first rule out a medial meniscus tear or MCL sprain with locking, swelling or giving way after a twist, arthritis with swelling and warmth, and pes anserine bursitis with a tender puffy spot below the joint. Muscle pain here is tender in the inner thigh muscles above the joint and reproduced by resisted knee straightening or squeezing the knees together, with no swelling. Kneecap pain is front and center, outside-of-knee pain follows the outer band from the hip.
inside-of-knee.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota golfer plays several rounds in a week on soft uneven fairways and adds a long day of kneeling to repot plants. A deep ache develops along the inside of one knee that makes the leg feel wobbly going downstairs. The joint is not swollen or locking, and pressing the teardrop muscle above the inner knee and the inner thigh reproduces the ache.

outside-of-knee.intro: Pain on the outside of the knee often feels like a sharp, burning ache or a tight band on the outer edge of the joint that comes on partway through a run or walk, sometimes with a snapping or rubbing sensation, and it tends to be worst going downhill or downstairs. People notice it after increasing running mileage, cycling with a low saddle, long beach walks on a slope, or sitting cross-legged for hours. The vastus lateralis, the large outer quadriceps muscle that straightens the knee, is the most common local source and refers pain to the outer joint. The tensor fasciae latae at the hip, which tightens the long outer band of the thigh, and the biceps femoris hamstring that attaches at the outer knee add ache along the same line.
outside-of-knee.differs: A physician should first rule out a lateral meniscus tear or LCL sprain with locking or giving way after a twist, arthritis with swelling and warmth, and a stress fracture of the outer shin bone in runners. Muscle-referred pain here is tender along the outer thigh and hip rather than on the joint line itself, and eases with rest. Kneecap pain is central and worse after sitting, inside-of-knee pain is on the opposite side and may feel like buckling.
outside-of-knee.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota runner training for a winter race increases mileage quickly and runs the sloped shoreline every morning facing the same way. A sharp burning ache appears on the outside of one knee a couple of miles in, worse running or walking downhill. The knee is not swollen or locking, and pressing the outer thigh and front-outer hip finds tender bands.

upper-calf.intro: Pain in the upper calf typically feels like a deep, cramp-like tightness in the thick part of the muscle just below the back of the knee, sometimes with a sudden night cramp or a sense that the calf is about to seize when pointing the toes.
