People notice it on the first steps in the morning, pushing off during a brisk walk, climbing stairs, or after a long day in flat sandals or high heels. The gastrocnemius, the large two-headed calf muscle that crosses the back of the knee and powers every push-off, is the most common source and holds tender bands that refer ache into the back of the knee and arch. The gluteus minimus at the hip can refer a line of ache down the back of the calf.
upper-calf.differs: A physician should first rule out a deep vein clot, especially with calf swelling, warmth, redness or recent travel or surgery, a muscle tear with bruising after a sudden pop, and arterial problems causing cramping that starts after a set walking distance. Muscle upper-calf pain is tender to pinch in the muscle belly and reproduced by rising onto the toes with a straight knee. Lower-calf pain sits down near the Achilles, and outer-calf pain runs along the outside of the shin.
upper-calf.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident swaps supportive shoes for flat flip-flops for the whole season and starts long walks along the bay. A deep cramping tightness sets into the upper calf that wakes them with a night cramp and tightens with the first steps each morning. There is no swelling, warmth or recent long travel, and pinching the calf muscle finds a tender band.

lower-calf.intro: Pain in the lower calf usually feels like a deep, dull ache or a tight, stiff sensation in the narrower part of the leg above the heel, often worst with the first steps in the morning, after a long sit, or when climbing stairs and hills, and it frequently travels into the heel and Achilles. People notice it after a sudden increase in walking or running, after a day on a ladder or on tiptoe, or after switching to flat shoes. The soleus, the broad, deep calf muscle under the gastrocnemius that works constantly to hold the body upright and powers slow walking, is the main source. The tibialis posterior, the deep muscle that supports the arch, adds ache along the inner lower calf.
lower-calf.differs: A physician should first rule out a deep vein clot with swelling, warmth, redness or recent travel, an Achilles tendon tear with a sudden pop and inability to push off, and arterial disease with cramping after a fixed walking distance. Muscle lower-calf pain is tender deep in the muscle and reproduced by rising onto the toes with the knee bent. Upper-calf pain is in the thick muscle belly near the knee, outer-calf pain follows the outside of the shin bone.
lower-calf.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident spends a week on a ladder hanging holiday lights and cleaning gutters, then walks daily on the hard-packed beach in flat sandals. A deep stiff ache settles into the lower calf above the heel that is worst with the first steps out of bed and climbing to the second floor. There is no swelling or sudden pop, and deep pressure in the calf finds the tender spot.

outer-calf.intro: Pain in the outer calf often feels like a dull ache or a tight line running down the outside of the lower leg between the shin bone and the calf, sometimes with a sense of weakness or instability at the outer ankle, and it is commonly noticed after walking on uneven ground, a rolled ankle, or a long stretch of standing on soft sand. The peroneals, the muscles along the outer shin that turn the foot outward and catch the body when the ankle starts to roll, are the usual local source and often stay tight for months after an ankle sprain. The gluteus minimus and piriformis, deep hip muscles that sit near the sciatic nerve, refer a line of ache down the outer calf that mimics sciatica.
outer-calf.differs: A physician should first rule out a stress fracture of the fibula in runners, a lumbar nerve root problem with numbness, weakness or foot drop, a peroneal nerve entrapment with tingling over the top of the foot, and a deep vein clot with swelling. Muscle outer-calf pain is tender along the outer shin muscles and reproduced by turning the foot outward against resistance. Upper-calf pain is in the thick muscle behind the knee, lower-calf pain sits above the heel.
outer-calf.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident rolls an ankle stepping off a boat dock, walks it off, then returns to long beach walks on soft, uneven sand within a few days. A dull ache sets in down the outside of the lower leg with a sense that the ankle might give again. Sensation on top of the foot is normal, there is no swelling of the calf, and pressing the outer shin muscles finds tender bands.

inner-ankle-and-arch.intro: Pain at the inner ankle and arch usually feels like a deep ache or a tired, collapsing sensation along the inside of the ankle bone and under the arch, often worst with the first steps in the morning, after standing a long time, or late in a long walk. People notice it after switching to flat, unsupportive sandals, a sudden increase in walking or running, or a long day on hard floors. The tibialis posterior, the deep calf muscle whose tendon wraps behind the inner ankle bone and holds up the arch, is the most common source. The small foot muscles under the arch, which grip the ground with every step, and the gastrocnemius and soleus in the calf refer ache into the arch as well.
inner-ankle-and-arch.differs: A physician should first rule out a posterior tibial tendon tear or dysfunction with a visibly collapsing arch, a fracture or ligament sprain after an injury, tarsal tunnel syndrome with burning or tingling in the sole, and arthritis with swelling. Muscle-referred pain here is tender along the inner calf and arch muscles and reproduced by rising onto the toes. Outer-ankle pain is on the opposite side, front-of-ankle pain is on top near the big toe, and sole pain sits under the heel.
inner-ankle-and-arch.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident spends the whole season in thin flip-flops and starts daily long walks on hard sidewalks, then stands for a weekend art festival. A deep tired ache develops along the inside of one ankle and under the arch, worst with the first steps each morning. There is no swelling or history of a twist, and pressing along the inner calf and arch finds tender spots.

outer-ankle.intro: Pain at the outer ankle often feels like a dull ache or a sharp twinge around and just below the outer ankle bone, sometimes with a sense that the ankle is weak or about to give way on uneven ground, and it is commonly noticed when stepping off a curb, walking on soft sand or gravel, or after a long stretch of standing. The peroneals, the muscles along the outside of the lower leg whose tendons wrap behind the outer ankle bone and stop the foot from rolling in, are the main source and frequently stay tight and tender long after a sprain has healed. The gluteus minimus at the hip can refer a line of ache all the way down the outer leg to the ankle.
outer-ankle.differs: A physician should first rule out a fracture or ligament tear after a sprain, especially with swelling, bruising or inability to bear weight, peroneal tendon tears or dislocation with snapping, arthritis, and a lumbar nerve problem with numbness. Muscle outer-ankle pain is tender along the outer calf muscles above the bone and reproduced by turning the foot outward against resistance. Inner-ankle pain is on the opposite side, front-of-ankle pain is on top, and sole pain is underneath.
outer-ankle.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident sprains an ankle on a shell-covered beach path, rests for a week, then goes straight back to long walks and standing on a rocking boat. A lingering ache sits around the outer ankle bone with a feeling that it could roll again. Swelling has resolved and weight bearing is fine, and pressing the muscles along the outer shin reproduces the ankle ache.

front-of-ankle.intro: Pain at the front of the ankle or big toe usually feels like a dull ache or a tight, pulling sensation across the front of the ankle crease and along the top of the foot toward the big toe, sometimes with a sense of a weak or slapping foot when walking. People notice it after a sudden increase in walking or running, hiking downhill, walking in soft sand, or driving long distances with the foot held on the pedal. The tibialis anterior, the muscle along the front of the shin that lifts the foot and toes with every step and controls the foot as it lands, is the primary source and refers pain down to the front of the ankle and the big toe.
front-of-ankle.differs: A physician should first rule out a stress fracture of the shin or foot, gout or arthritis in the big toe joint with redness, swelling and heat, a nerve problem with numbness or true foot drop, and anterior compartment syndrome with hard swelling after exertion. Muscle pain here is tender along the front of the shin and reproduced by lifting the foot against resistance. Inner-ankle pain is on the inside below the bone, outer-ankle pain is on the outside, and sole pain is underneath the heel.
front-of-ankle.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident drives a long distance south with the right foot flexed on the pedal for hours, then begins daily walks in deep soft sand. A dull pulling ache develops across the front of the ankle and toward the big toe, worse after long walks and on waking. The toe joint is not red or swollen, and pressing along the front of the shin reproduces the ankle ache.

sole-of-foot.intro: Pain in the sole of the foot usually feels like a deep bruise or a sharp stab under the heel or through the arch, famously worst with the first steps out of bed in the morning and again after sitting for a while, then easing as the foot warms up. People notice it after a sudden increase in standing or walking, after switching to flat, unsupportive sandals, or after gaining weight or returning to exercise. The small intrinsic foot muscles, the layers of muscle under the arch that grip the ground and spring the foot forward, are the most common local source. The gastrocnemius and soleus in the calf, which pull on the heel through the Achilles, and the tibialis posterior refer ache into the arch and heel as well.
sole-of-foot.differs: A physician should first rule out a heel stress fracture, a true plantar fascia tear with sudden pain and bruising, tarsal tunnel syndrome with burning or tingling, gout or arthritis with a hot swollen joint, and nerve problems linked to diabetes. Muscle-referred sole pain is tender deep in the arch and calf and eases as the foot warms up. Inner-ankle pain is up along the inside of the ankle, outer-ankle pain is on the outside bone, and front-of-ankle pain is on top near the big toe.
sole-of-foot.scenario: Typical story: a Sarasota resident starts a new job standing all day on tile, lives in flat flip-flops, and adds evening walks on the hard sidewalk. A deep bruised stab develops under one heel with the first steps every morning that eases after a few minutes, then returns after sitting through lunch. There is no swelling or heat, and pressing the arch and calf finds tender spots.
